# Document Structure Every HTML5 document has a specific skeleton. ```html Page Title

Hello World

``` - ``: Tells the browser this is an HTML5 document. - ``: The root element. - ``: Contains metadata (not visible to users). - ``: Contains the visible content.

lessons.title: Semantic Elements
lessons.content:
# Semantic Elements

Semantic elements clearly describe their meaning to both the browser and the developer.

### Why use them?
- **Accessibility**: Screen readers use them to navigate.
- **SEO**: Search engines understand the page structure better.

### Common Semantic Tags
- `<header>`: Header for a document or section.
- `<nav>`: Container for navigation links.
- `<main>`: Main content of the document.
- `<article>`: Independent, self-contained content.
- `<section>`: Thematic grouping of content.
- `<footer>`: Footer for a document or section.

lessons.title: Forms & Inputs
lessons.content:
# Forms & Inputs

Used to collect user input.

```html
<form action="/submit" method="POST">
  <label for="name">Name:</label>
  <input type="text" id="name" name="name">
  
  <input type="submit" value="Submit">
</form>
```

### Input Types
- `text`, `password`, `email`, `number`
- `checkbox`, `radio`
- `date`, `color`, `file`

lessons.title: Meta Tags
lessons.content:
# Meta Tags

Provide metadata about the HTML document. They go inside the `<head>` element.

```html
<meta name="description" content="Free Web tutorials">
<meta name="keywords" content="HTML, CSS, JavaScript">
<meta name="author" content="John Doe">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
```
The `viewport` meta tag is essential for responsive design on mobile devices.

lessons.title: Scripts & Links
lessons.content:
# Scripts & Links

### Linking CSS
```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css">
```

### Adding JavaScript
```html
<script src="script.js"></script>
```
It's often recommended to place `<script>` tags at the end of the `<body>` or use `defer`/`async` to prevent blocking the page render.

lessons.title: HTML5 Canvas & SVG
lessons.content:
# HTML5 Canvas & SVG

### Canvas
Used to draw graphics on the fly via JavaScript.
```html
<canvas id="myCanvas" width="200" height="100"></canvas>
```

### SVG (Scalable Vector Graphics)
Defines vector-based graphics in XML format. They are scalable and do not lose quality when resized.
```html
<svg width="100" height="100">
  <circle cx="50" cy="50" r="40" stroke="green" stroke-width="4" fill="yellow" />
</svg>
```
